articleTitle: IEE Colloquium on 'Radiation Protection - the Role of Safety-Related Control Systems' (Digest No.156)
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Radiation Protection - the Role of Safety-Related Control Systems
IEE Colloquium on Radiation Protection - the Role of Safety-Related Control Systems
abstract: Radiation sources of a wide range of type and energy are used extensively throughout industry, research, medicine, educational establishments and the public domain. Sealed source activities range from a few kilo Bequerels in smoke detectors to terra Bequerels in irradiation plants for sterilisation of medical equipment. X-rays sources range in energy from a hundred kilo electron volts for dental X-ray equipment to hundreds of millions of electron volts in research accelerators. Aspects of standards, cooperation and legislation are discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Radiation Protection - the Role of Safety-Related Control Systems
abstract: Developing high integrity systems involves applying good practice, using software engineering discipline, and gaining the assurance of an independent assessment of the work. The project should have a safety plan which includes a hazard analysis, a clear statement of the safety requirements and the use of safety oriented design and analysis techniques. It may not be possible for one individual working on a small project to apply these techniques effectively. At some stage it will be necessary to call for assistance from another with the relevant experience. This is another way of saying that safety critical software should be given the attention of the necessary specialist.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Radiation Protection - the Role of Safety-Related Control Systems
abstract: The author discusses regulations and guidelines for the use of ionising radiations in various processing facilities: chemical processing, physical processing and food irradiation treatment. Hazard analysis and safety philosophies are examined.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Radiation Protection - the Role of Safety-Related Control Systems
abstract: The author concentrates on the main aspects of civil law which relate to radiation systems. Under civil law there are three main areas of potential liability namely contract, tort (specifically the tort of negligence) and product liability. Each of these is dealt with in turn.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: International and European standards for safety-related systems
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Radiation Protection - the Role of Safety-Related Control Systems
abstract: The authors provide a brief overview of standards being developed internationally, in the IEC (International Electrotechnical Commission) and within Europe in CEN (European Committee for Standardisation) and CENELEC (European Committee for Electrical Standardisation), to meet the requirements of the Machinery Directive.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
